The studio

We treat paint the way restorers treat gilding — as the last, most visible act of architecture.

We work in small crews, one project at a time. A single foreman stays with a house from the first survey to the final coat, so nothing is handed off and nothing is hurried.

Surfaces are diagnosed before they are dressed. We read the substrate, the moisture, the old sheens beneath, then let the cure times set the schedule rather than the other way around.

  • Preparation

    Nine-tenths of the hours are spent before the first coat — filling, sanding, sealing, until the wall is quieter than the paint that will cover it.

  • Pigment

    Full-bodied mineral paints, mixed to the light of the room. We sample each colour on the actual surface and watch it through a full day before we commit.

  • Patience

    Schedules bend to cure times, not the reverse. A finish left to settle properly outlasts one rushed to a deadline by a decade or more.

Services

Four disciplines, one standard.

From a first coat on new plaster to gilded detail restored by hand — the same crew, the same finish schedule, the same patience throughout.

Interiors

Rooms finished to be lived in

Walls, ceilings, trim and millwork carried through in full-bodied mineral finishes. Every room is masked, dust-sealed and worked under a furniture-safe site protocol, so the house stays a home while we are in it.

Enquire →

Exteriors

Facades built to weather

Facades, render, joinery and ironwork, each treated as its own problem. Systems are specified against weather and time rather than the calendar, so a coat laid this spring is still holding a decade of seasons later.

Enquire →

Fine Finishes

The atelier work we are named for

Lacquer, limewash, Venetian plaster, cabinetry and gilded detail, built up in coats and burnished by hand. This is the slow, quiet craft the studio was founded on, reserved for surfaces that deserve it.

Color Consultation

A sitting with our colorists

Light studies through the day, colours brushed out large on sample boards, and a written finish schedule you keep. You leave knowing exactly how each surface will read, in your own rooms, in your own light.

The process

Slow is a schedule, not an accident.

Five stages, in order, each allowed the time it asks for. Nothing on a Vermeil project is hurried into place.

01

Consultation

We walk the rooms with you, in the light they actually live in. Scope and honesty first, before a single price is spoken.

02

Specification

A written finish schedule — colours, sheens, systems, cure times. Nothing on site is improvised, and nothing is left to memory.

03

Preparation

Protection, repair, fill, sand, prime. Nine-tenths of the hours no one ever sees, spent making the wall quieter than the paint to come.

04

Application

Small master crews, thin coats, long cures. Brushwork where brushwork belongs, and a straight roller where it does not.

05

The Reveal

Furniture returned to the millimetre, a final walkthrough together, and an aftercare dossier you keep for the life of the finish.
